Scope: Local dynamic finite-field point dispatcher before Tianhe deployment; no remote jobs affected
Observed: Initial dispatcher froze only the executable; subprocess arguments still referenced development JSON files. Diagnostic options were added to those source files during completed/active diagnostic batches. Original executables ignored the new options, but the recorded startup hash alone did not freeze runtime reads.
Cause: Hash-only input identity was used without staging the actual files passed to numerical workers.
Correction: Stage family, basis and targets into the unique run/input directory, verify their hashes, and pass those frozen paths to every worker. Preserve valid point data. Recover the completed minimal44 input snapshot byte-for-byte and verify against its original SHA256.
GeneralLesson: A startup source hash is not an immutable runtime input. Freeze and validate the actual file paths supplied to workers, separately from source review and binary freezing.
Validation: Actual freeze_input function regression changes the source after staging and confirms the worker input copy is unchanged; dynamic dispatch regressions passed. Recovered minimal44 snapshot matches original SHA256; independent eight-point physical checks pass.
